Twelve dogs were in the play yard during inspection and did not have water available for them to drink. When asked, the
licensee stated they had been in the yard for approximately an hour. I asked the licensee to provide the dogs with a bowl
of water. He brought the dogs out two water bowls and at least 11 of the 12 dogs crowded the bowls. At one point, one of
the dogs was trying to (and successfully) pawed one of the water bowls away from the rest of the dogs.
Not having water continuously available may negatively affect the health and well being of the dogs. The dogs must be
provided potable water on a continual basis. Correct starting on 9/25/26.

The program of veterinary care doesn't have a schedule of how many (or what percentage of dogs) must be sampled for
heartworm and fecal parasites. Not having a written schedule approved by the attending veterinarian doesn't allow for
APHIS officials to be able to determine if the correct number of dogs are being sampled for these parasites on a yearly
basis. The program of veterinary care must document the sampling and treatment of the various parasites in accordance
with a schedule that has been approved by the attending veterinarian. Correct by 10/9/26.

The licensee has heartworm tested and fecal tested a percentage of their adult population, but they do not have the
documentation of the heartworm or fecal test results for these dogs. Not having records of all routine test results doesn't
allow APHIS officials to be able to review and ensure these tests have been conducted in accordance with the schedule
that is in the program of veterinary care. The licensee must keep records of all routine test results that are done on all
dogs. Correct starting on 9/25/26.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
